title: Ссора у туалета и постоянная клиентка  (Restroom Clash and the Regular Client)

segments.t: Outside the guest restroom, Vika blocks Chef Barinov and tells him that as head chef he should stop this childish circus, while Viktor Petrovich retorts that he is not cooking inside the bathroom. Back in the kitchen, Kostya jokes about how fast Max satisfies his regular lady guest.
Правда, идет?
Вам сюда нельзя.
Вика, ты прекращай этот цирк.
Витя, ты шеф-повар этого ресторана.
Ты думаешь, нормально?
Ну я же мне в туалете еду готовил.
Пойдем на кухню.
Это же мой первый постоянный клиент.
Понял? Ну?
Скажи две минуты, и все будет готово.
Так посмотри, какой мужчина.
За две минуты может удовлетворить женщину.
Иди давай, а.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Правда, идет?
'Does it really suit me?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'honestly', while 'goes' completes the thought.
Вам сюда нельзя.
'You are not allowed in here.' Vika chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'must not' to keep a polite distance. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Вика, ты прекращай этот цирк.
'Vika, stop this circus right now.' The grammar packs 'Vika' and 'circus' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Витя, ты шеф-повар этого ресторана.
'Vitya, you are the head chef of this restaurant.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'Vitya' and 'you' in a few short words.
Ты думаешь, нормально?
'Do you think this behavior is normal?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Chef Barinov's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
Ну я же мне в туалете еду готовил.
'Well, I was not cooking food inside the restroom.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'was preparing' without extra filler words.
Пойдем на кухню.
'Let us go back to the kitchen.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'let's go' and 'on' in a few short words.
Это же мой первый постоянный клиент.
'She is my very first regular client.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'client' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Понял? Ну?
'Got it? Well?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'understood?' places the action in the masculine past tense.
Скажи две минуты, и все будет готово.
'Tell her two minutes and everything will be ready.' Vika anchors the line on 'say', while 'ready' completes the thought.
Так посмотри, какой мужчина.
'Just look at what a man he is.' In Russian, the idea of 'like this' flows naturally into 'man' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
За две минуты может удовлетворить женщину.
'He can satisfy a woman in two minutes flat.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'behind' before landing on 'a woman'.
Иди давай, а.
'Oh, get out of here already.' The grammar packs 'go' and 'and' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.

That wraps up this scene as vika catches Chef Barinov trying to use the dining room restroom and demands he stop the circus, while Kostya teases Max for satisfying his older regular client in two minutes. Until next time!
Всего хорошего!
